failure_reason: It categorically says 'No further test extension is warranted' and 'more waiting has no decision value' merely because the CI clears breakeven, despite a pending validity audit and uninspected sensitivity grid. That assurance exceeds what the conditional projection establishes.

The prose says the lottery ITT needs only independence, but the reduced-form code says it requires independence plus exclusion. This contradiction obscures that the effect of assignment can remain useful even when lottery-induced schooling invalidates the service LATE.

The ITT discussion repeatedly requires exclusion as well as independence, although it defines ITT as the effect of drawing a number, including any effects through schooling or career changes. It therefore misses why assignment effects remain useful when the service-only exclusion restriction fails.

It introduces difference-in-discontinuities as a third, "stronger option" but gives no limitation of that approach; merely having a pre-existing score threshold does not establish that its pre-existing earnings jump is stable enough to subtract.

The proposed difference-in-discontinuities option has no corresponding assumptions discussion, notably no explanation that the pre-existing earnings discontinuity must remain stable absent the algorithm change.

The script fits `feols()` to the all-zero missing-outcome indicator before fitting ITT or CACE. That constant-outcome regression stops execution, so the supplied code never reaches its side-by-side results table on the described complete data.

The combined ITT/CACE summary appears after a permutation loop whose `feols(df$outcome ~ perm_assign)` call omits the required `data` argument. Execution stops in that loop, so the code does not reach its combined comparison output.

The proposed first diagnostic uses a "2-year pre-period," but the supplied two-year history includes six months after launch. The plan therefore asks for a pre-treatment window that the available data cannot provide and overstates the baseline used to choose the method.

The fallback rematches with `replace = TRUE` but still estimates uncertainty with `vcov = ~subclass` on `match.data(m_out)`. Replacement matching does not supply that pair-subclass column, so the advertised fallback fails at effect estimation rather than completing the analysis.

The holdout and residual gate tests a fixed ARIMA(1,d,0), but the effect stage discards that specification and calls CausalArima with auto=True. Passing those diagnostics therefore does not validate the counterfactual model that actually produces the reported effect.

The permutation loop calls `feols(df$outcome ~ perm_assign)` without the required `data` argument. This aborts the supplied script before its final ITT/CACE summary, so the complete analysis is not runnable as written.

All 2,000 outcomes are observed, so `missing_outcome` is identically zero. The unguarded `feols(missing_outcome ~ assigned_treatment, ...)` rejects a constant dependent variable and stops the script before either ITT or CACE is fitted.
The permutation loop calls `feols(df$outcome ~ perm_assign)` without the required `data` argument. It therefore aborts before the final summary instead of providing a complete runnable analysis.

The scenario says kiosk installation started in year two of the 24-month history, but the generator assigns the first rollout wave to month 7. The data therefore contradict the business rollout timeline the student is asked to analyze.
